findings.summary: Unbriefed over-limit findings now reach no surface
findings.evidence: This follows the accepted reading and is documented as a tradeoff in D169 and 'Left for later'. A finding at a design rung that the steward cannot fix and does not brief is recorded, then only found by its id.

summary: The change does what the accepted reading asks, and code now enforces the routing. decide() never applies a briefed change: it records it as a Proposed item of kind proposal at any rung. An unbriefed change is applied when within the limit and only recorded above it. open_proposals, in_limit and the decisions page list a proposal only when it has a brief, except for unbriefed in-limit items, which stay listed for the drain. A new blind_spot_needing_owner gives a missing-GH_TOKEN blind spot a brief. Its own key keeps an earlier plain github blind spot from hiding it. The steward prompt (role version 3) carries the step-back, decide-yourself and brief-only-for-env/token wording, marked prose-only, and a test composes the real prompt within 600 tokens. I ran the targeted tests in athena-core, athena-cli (steward), athena-data, athena-context and xtask, and all pass. fmt, clippy and the full test suite were recorded as passing by CI. Athena's fails-without runs show the new tests fail without the fix. The findings are minor. Four planned files sit outside the expected-deliverables list. docs/spec.toml still describes the old routing. Three open briefed proposals in the real records, written under the old v2 rule, will still reach the owner (seen in the read-only evidence snapshot).
